newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah falls on dollar short-covering.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah falls on dollar short-covering.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah fell against the dollar in active late Tuesday trading on continued short-covering by London operators, dealers said.
They said the rupiah started to fall after the London market opened, on continued dollar short-covering after speculation of a central bank band widening did not materialise.
"It's mainly a follow-through from Monday's short-covering as speculation on the band seemed to crumble," one dealer said.
Dealers said London operators were getting nervous late on Monday as they could not find counter party because the Jakarta market had closed, driving the rupiah down to a low of 2,383.0.
Spot rupiah was quoted at 2,377.0/78.0 at 0930 GMT against an opening of 2,371.0/72.0. Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,372.0/72.6 and 2,372.25/73.00, respectively.
One foreign bank dealer said the fall could have been more severe if there was less profit-taking by local operators who went long last Friday following offshore speculation.
Tom/next swap fell to -0.3 points. Overnight swap was last at -0.1/par. However, longer-term swaps were seen recovering slightly after offshore players started to buy back.
Overnight money fell to five percent in the afternoon from six percent. The central bank did not offer overnight papers.
One local bank dealer said he expected the market to only stabilise on Thursday. "There will be still some carry-forward impact on Wednesday," the dealer said.
Overnight dollar deposit rates rose further to nine percent from 8.5 percent because the market dried up on operators' selling of some $1.1 billion to the central bank last Friday.
"Local operators are calm. It seems that the nervous ones are offshore players who might have suffered a lot due to the failed speculation on the band," the dealer said.
Operators who maintained short positions were squeezed in the swap market, with short-term rates falling below par.
The central bank raised its intervention band by one point to 2,365/2,557 and the conversion band also by one point to 2,364/2,412 on Tuesday, the second rise in the week.
Offshore operators started heavy speculation last Friday that a central bank widenening of its band was imminent.
The speculation triggered heavy dollar selling because any band widening in the past had caused the rupiah to strengthen.
Broad-based dollar selling sent the dollar falling three points below the floor rate of the band.
But until late on Tuesday, the speculation had not yet materialised, forcing many players to cut losses.
One-month swap was at 10.50/11.25, two at 21.0/22.5, three at 32.5/33.5 and six at 73.5/74.5 points.
